160.title: Use Factory's implementation unless a project overrides it
160.description:
Projects should use Factory's standard implementation without copying or maintaining its workflow code. Keep ordinary customization in validated project settings and additive instruction files; projects that need different stages or code-owned defaults explicitly supply a complete Sandcastle workflow instead. Model configuration selects one OpenAI or Anthropic family for the project, with Pi as the only standard agent.

**In scope**

- Factory-owned runtime by default for new projects, used consistently by manual runs, dispatch, scheduling, refresh and recovery.
- Explicit whole-workflow code overrides, never implicit per-file replacement or mixed module ownership.
- Project-wide model family, default OpenAI; Factory-owned model mappings and Small/Mid/Large ticket tiers, default Mid.
- Preserve existing ordinary tracker, selection, dispatch, merge, analysis, CI and sandbox settings, except superseded model/agent configuration.
- Additive project instruction files and read-only effective-configuration reporting.
- Immutable runtime identity for active executions, regression coverage, and a final user/agent documentation task.

**Out of scope**

- Existing-project compatibility, automatic conversion, migration tooling or migrating real projects. The owner will migrate manually after this lands.
- Configurable stages, individual module overrides, arbitrary lifecycle hooks or full Factory-prompt replacement.
- Configurable individual models, model aliases, agent implementations, per-role families, thinking levels or new execution-deadline settings. Those require a code override.
- Relaxing verification, delivery, admission or recovery-budget safeguards; adding sandbox resource/network settings or a dashboard.
- Per-project Factory version pins, automatic runtime garbage collection or changes to the user's installed services and credentials during implementation.

**Estimate:** 90h (human, without AI)

Implementation is split into seven child tasks. The configuration audit, agreed Q&A, complete plan and task/dependency index are in the comments. The final child task documents the finished system for users and agents.
comments:
<details>
<summary>Q&A</summary>

**Q1. How should existing projects adopt the shared runtime?**
Ignore existing projects for this change. The owner will migrate them manually after it lands. Compatibility, conversion and migration tooling are out of scope.

**Q2. Include the proposed configuration additions, rather than only relocating code?**
Yes, subject to the narrower model and deadline decisions below.

**Q3. Should projects replace a whole workflow or individual installed modules?**
Use an explicit whole-workflow override, without per-module mixing. The owner requested examples before answering, then chose the complete-workflow boundary.

**Q4. Should projects configure models and agents independently per role?**
No. Projects configure model families only: OpenAI or Anthropic, through Pi providers openai or pi-claude-subscription. Individual models require a code override. Pi is the only standard agent.

**Q5. Add implementation, verification and recovery deadline settings?**
No. Those changes belong in code. Do not add deadline configuration in this epic.

**Q6. Proceed with filing the epic and tasks, and how should documentation be scheduled?**
Confirmed. The last task must carefully explain the finished system to users and agents.

**Q7. One family per project or different families by role, and which default?**
One family for the entire standard workflow. Default OpenAI.

**Q8. How do ticket model declarations interact with Factory-owned model choices?**
Use Small/Mid/Large ticket tiers, default Mid. Reject explicit model-ID declarations with actionable guidance.

</details>
## Configuration audit and recommendation

Investigated source baseline: `ac928a809ac86b748e58c241d937dbed554d7d04`. This is a source-code audit, not a claim about the version any installed project runs. The final decisions below supersede the initial suggestion of per-role model and deadline configuration.

### Configurable today

The current version-1 contract is documented in `docs/project-config.md` and implemented by `orchestrator/project-config.mts`.

| Area | Current settings and defaults |
| --- | --- |
| Tracker | Required kind/project; GitHub host defaults to github.com; GitLab requires host/project_id |
| Selection | Milestone, assignee, author, tracker-native search, excluded assignees; GitLab issue_type/confidential |
| Labels | Required needs_human/done; selection all defaults to ready-for-agent; none defaults to blocked/needs-human/wontfix |
| Ordering | created/asc by default; updated/popularity on both trackers, additional GitLab order keys |
| Work units | subtasks by default, or whole issues; invocation can override |
| Dispatch | max_concurrent=3 across shared active runs/reservations, stagger_seconds=20; invocation can override cap |
| Agent/model | Required claude/pi provider, fixed verifier/recovery model, approved alias map; optional Pi thinking |
| Implementer | Ticket description must declare Model or Pi model; missing, unsupported or conflicting declarations hold work. No configured fallback |
| Merge | auto=false, method=squash, required_checks=[]; profiles override auto and labels |
| Analysis | Required graph.model; max_analyses_per_pass=5, analysis_timeout_minutes=10, conflict_ignore=[], prune_after_days=30 |
| CI | wait_minutes=30, no_pipeline_minutes=5 |
| Sandbox | Required image; setup=[]; ordered command steps with optional timeout_ms and sudo=false |

All eligibility axes combine with AND. GitLab-only options fail on GitHub. Unknown keys and invalid values fail before execution. A present TOML file owns ordinary settings, without per-field legacy fallback. Without TOML, the current code still executes legacy config/SELECT/CONFIG behavior. Credentials stay outside TOML.

The machine registry, saved scheduler Node/PATH, service configuration, agent authentication, subscription-extension location and shared state directory are operational inputs, not new project settings to duplicate in this epic. Existing CLI overrides such as --max, --whole-issues and --no-push remain explicit invocation controls.

### Why projects still carry implementation code

- `cli/src/scaffold.mts` copies main/dispatch, tracker adapters, analysis/recovery/verification helpers, Board/admission helpers, parser and prompts into `.sandcastle/`.
- `cli/src/commands/run.mts` and `dispatch.mts` run the project's `dispatch.sh`.
- `cli/src/commands/tick.mts`, `cli/src/schedule.mts`, `board/refresh-worker.mts`, `cli/src/recovery-run.mts` and `cli/src/recovery-review.mts` discover or inspect those copied files.
- `orchestrator/runtime-config.mts` loads configuration relative to its module, so merely pointing the CLI at installed `main.mts` would read the wrong project settings.
- `orchestrator/main.mts`, `handoff.mts`, `analyze.mts` and `recovery.mts` embed project-relative prompt paths. Dispatch also spawns project-local main.mts and installs runtime dependencies in the project's node_modules.
- `cli/src/update.mts` protects customized code and prompts. This is reasonable for a copied workflow, but makes routine Factory bug fixes a project-copy upgrade exercise.

A default-runtime change must therefore cover every launch path, dependencies, configuration roots, prompt/helper paths and recovery review. Deleting copied main.mts alone is not enough.

### Agreed configuration boundary

| Keep or add as data | Keep in Factory code, override by owning a workflow |
| --- | --- |
| Existing tracker/selection/labels/work/dispatch/merge/CI settings | Stage order, stage definitions and arbitrary lifecycle hooks |
| Existing sandbox image/setup commands and project helper scripts | Individual models, aliases, Pi implementation selection and thinking policy |
| Existing non-model graph controls, including current analysis timeout | New implementation/verification/recovery deadline controls, iteration/retry policy |
| One `agent.family`: openai by default, or anthropic | Exact tier/role-to-model mappings |
| `workflow.mode`: factory by default, or explicit project directory | Partial module overrides and mixed installed/project helpers |
| Additive common/role instruction file lists | Replacement Factory templates or verifier output/proof contracts |
| Read-only resolved configuration and runtime identity | Admission fencing, proof authority, delivery SHA gates and recovery accounting |

Pi provider mapping is fixed: openai -> `openai`, anthropic -> `pi-claude-subscription`. Direct Claude Code is not a standard workflow agent. Claude Code can still be the subscription provider's internal implementation; that does not make it a project-selectable agent.

Tickets use `**Model tier:** small|mid|large`, matched case-insensitively. No declaration defaults to Mid. Exact `Model`/`Pi model` declarations fail with guidance to use Model tier. Ticket text never selects a different family or a custom model. The initial Factory-owned mappings are the current ticket-planning Small/Mid/Large models: OpenAI gpt-6-luna/gpt-6.1-terra/gpt-6.1-sol, Anthropic claude-haiku-5-5/claude-sonnet-5-5/claude-opus-5-5 through pi-claude-subscription. Analysis uses Mid; verification and recovery use Large. Thinking remains code-owned at high, matching the existing personal Pi policy. These defaults are explicit code, not project configuration.

### What should not be added now

No stage builder, plugin framework, generic hooks, arbitrary environment/secret interpolation, network/resource policy editor, model-ID escape hatch, per-project version pins or migration engine. Keep current timeouts where they already exist; do not add new deadline settings. Additive instructions cannot authorize weaker proof, different host tools or automatic delivery.

### Related tickets

- #137 delivered TOML configuration and selection explanation. Reuse its validation and data-only loading patterns, but the new breaking schema replaces agent/model ownership.
- #156 proposes local source/app/project drift reporting. This epic's config explanation reports only the selected runtime/config contract; it does not duplicate drift/image inspection. No hard dependency on #156.
- #149 changes dependency evaluation. Preserve its fail-closed semantics when moving execution.
- #151 introduces recovery preparation. Runtime routing must include that helper and retain pre-charge checks once it lands.
- #152 introduces image readiness. Preserve the mandatory capability probe in both normal and recovery launch paths once it lands.
- #153 introduces delivery follow-up. The routed dispatcher must retain the same checkpoint/proof/current-schedule checks once it lands.
- #155 changes documentation policy. Follow the effective repository policy; the final comprehensive documentation task remains last regardless.

These existing tickets do not need changes just because files overlap. Their current ready-for-agent plans were reviewed. This epic does not require their new features to implement a shared runtime, so file overlap alone is not a blocker. Its acceptance suite must retain any contracts present on the implementation base.

### Proposed work order

1. Breaking schema and Factory-owned model/tier policy.
2. Installed, content-addressed runtime bundles and dependency ownership.
3. Project-root-aware standard workflow execution.
4. Consistent CLI/scheduler/Board routing and explicit complete-workflow overrides.
5. Minimal new-project assets and additive instructions.
6. Read-only effective configuration and cross-path acceptance tests.
7. Final user/agent guide after all implementation tasks.

Existing projects are deliberately not a compatibility target. Reject unsupported old inputs with manual-migration guidance; never silently infer that an old customized workflow is the new default. Do not rewrite, delete or migrate real project files as part of this work.
<details>
<summary>Implementation plan</summary>

## Approach

Separate Factory-owned executable code from project-owned data. Install a complete content-addressed runtime with its own dependencies; select it once per workflow invocation. Resolve project configuration, logs, helper scripts and workspaces from a canonical project root, never from the installed module directory. New projects contain only data and optional project assets. An explicit complete-workflow directory is the only way to replace code. Fixed stages and existing host safety contracts remain intact.

This is a breaking new-project contract. Use schema version 2. Version 1 and absent TOML are unsupported by the new shared workflow and fail with manual-migration guidance, not executable fallback. Do not implement a converter, legacy compatibility layer or deployed-project migration. Do not delete real existing files. The parent is an orchestration container, not an extra implementation job.

## Configuration contract

Preserve all current non-AI tables, semantics and default values from docs/project-config.md, including the existing graph.analysis_timeout_minutes, setup timeout_ms and CI waits. Replace the agent table with optional `agent.family = "openai" | "anthropic"`, default openai. Remove graph.model and agent.provider/model/thinking/model_aliases from accepted v2 data. Unknown and superseded keys fail with key-specific guidance. No per-role settings or new deadline keys.

Add optional `[workflow]`: mode=factory by default, or project. `directory` is required only in project mode and rejected in factory mode. It is a repository-relative directory whose real path stays inside the canonical checkout. Reject absolute paths, parent traversal, dangling links and links escaping the checkout. A configured override must contain a complete runtime inventory and manifest under the contract below. In factory mode local main/dispatch/helpers/prompts are never executable overrides, even if present.

Add optional `[instructions]` arrays named common, implementation, verification, analysis and recovery. Each defaults to []. Values are nonempty repository-relative Markdown file paths, resolved and validated before an agent starts. Validate every component and real path against checkout containment; reject directories, missing files and escaping symlinks. Preserve list order; apply common followed by role-specific entries, deduplicating the same canonical file at first occurrence. A role is not a stage-definition hook. Model policy, deadlines, host tools and proof requirements cannot be replaced by these files.

## Model policy

Add pure `orchestrator/model-policy.mts`. All standard agents are Pi. OpenAI family maps to Pi openai; Anthropic maps to pi-claude-subscription. Code-owned implementer tiers:

| Tier | OpenAI | Anthropic |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Small | openai/gpt-6-luna | pi-claude-subscription/claude-haiku-5-5 |
| Mid | openai/gpt-6.1-terra | pi-claude-subscription/claude-sonnet-5-5 |
| Large | openai/gpt-6.1-sol | pi-claude-subscription/claude-opus-5-5 |

Analysis uses Mid; verification and recovery use Large. Code-owned thinking is high, preserving the current personal Pi policy. No model probing, automatic fallback or provider switching. Preserve explicit subscription-extension loading and read-only analysis tools. Failure to provision a selected model/provider is an actionable hold, never a reason to use another model.

Change ticket parsing to recognize standalone `Model tier:` or `**Model tier:**` with one case-insensitive small/mid/large value. Reuse existing exclusion of code fences, indented code, quotes and HTML comments. No field resolves Mid with source=factory-default. Identical duplicate tiers are accepted; conflicting tiers or unsupported values hold. Active Model/Pi model declarations, including old aliases and full IDs, hold with guidance to use Model tier; do not reinterpret an old model name as a tier. Parent text, comments, labels and prose do not select tiers. Description revision, family, tier, full resolved model and source are frozen at attempt start. Recovery uses its code-owned role default, not the old implementer tier.

## Runtime ownership and identity

Add `cli/src/runtime-assets.mts` for the single complete runtime inventory and assembly mapping, and `cli/src/runtime-bundle.mts` for installation. Assemble a flat runtime directory from orchestrator modules, required board helpers, vendored parser and Factory prompts. The current scaffold copy lists are the starting inventory, not a second permanent source of truth. Include every transitive executable helper present on the implementation base, including newly landed dependency/preparation/capability/delivery helpers. Factory's default prompt sources are cli/templates/project/prompt.md, cli/templates/project/prompt.verify.md and orchestrator/prompt.analyze.md/prompt.recover.md. Project-specific source examples in orchestrator/main/config must not leak into new defaults.

Use `<Factory data>/runtimes/<content-id>/` with package.json/package-lock.json and a private node_modules. Copy the root locked runtime dependencies for @ai-hero/sandcastle and tsx into bundle preparation, install with npm ci --include=dev --ignore-scripts inside an unpublished temporary bundle, then publish atomically. Do not use target-project npm/npx resolution or install dependencies into projects. Record manifest version, sorted relative source-file hashes, lockfile hash, Node compatibility and content identity. The identity is a content identity, not invented release/signature provenance. Validate source/lock inventory before launch. Never edit a published bundle in place.

Write an atomic installed-app runtime descriptor identifying the complete bundle. Factory install publishes a new bundle before changing this descriptor, leaves the previous descriptor usable on failure, and keeps old bundles. Existing p.app installation layout may remain; runtime paths are outside the replaceable app directory. Both copied and --link installs build/select a bundle. Link mode updates require reinstall to publish a new runtime, not live mutation of executable code beneath an active run. No per-project version pins or automatic garbage collection. Integrate the runtime store with ownership/uninstall validation; never delete live referenced bundles. Runtime leases use current PID/start-identity ownership patterns, not unsafe age-based lock theft. Tests use local prepared/stub dependency trees and never access a package registry.

## Project-aware execution context

Add `orchestrator/context.mts` with explicit canonical project root, selected runtime root/identity, project asset directory, shared state directory and normalized settings. Trusted launchers provide absolute FACTORY_PROJECT_ROOT and FACTORY_RUNTIME_ROOT, and retain project-root cwd for Git operations. Context rejects mismatches and never infers the project from the runtime directory. Propagate these values to all detached children. For direct low-level entrypoints, missing context fails with guidance to use Factory CLI rather than guessing a different project.

Change runtime-config.mts to load v2 data from the context's project directory. No legacy import fallback. Change main.mts, dispatch.mts, dispatch.sh, analyze.mts, refresh.mts, preflight/config-read, handoff.mts and recovery modules to distinguish code/template paths from project asset paths. Static imports always come from the selected complete runtime. Prompt files come from runtime root; .env, logs, evidence, sandbox helpers and worktrees remain project-owned under canonical project paths. Do not redesign their layout in this epic. Dependency binaries come from the selected runtime, with absolute paths, never project npx. Dispatch children retain the same bundle as their parent pass even if a reinstall publishes another bundle. Fresh invocations select the newest installed descriptor; an active attempt never changes its family/model/prompt snapshot midway.

Preserve all existing stages and their gates. Current proof identity must bind the actual runtime inventory, normalized safety-relevant config and frozen instruction/template bytes. Configuration or instruction changes still invalidate relevant analysis/proof before delivery; no new setting may make old verification authorize new requirements. Keep admission, attempt charging, cleanup, image probes, browser requirements and exact-SHA merge checks unchanged. Where #151/#152/#153 features have landed, resolve those helpers through the same selected runtime.

## Complete project override

Add import-safe `orchestrator/workflow.mts` for data-only selection and inventory validation, usable by CLI and Board without importing the workflow's code. Inputs are canonical project root and the installed runtime descriptor. Output identifies mode/root/content identity and the fixed entrypoints. In project mode require the same versioned manifest shape, complete runtime inventory, package/lock metadata and local dependencies. Recompute source hashes to identify edited project code; export/copy instructions explain updating its manifest after edits. Reject incomplete/unknown manifests or entrypoints outside the selected directory. A bad selected override fails without calling installed helpers as a fallback.

A complete override can start as a copy of a published Factory bundle and owns its code and dependencies. It is trusted project code, not a security sandbox. The manifest identifies executable ownership, not permission to bypass host admission/proof rules. Project-mode recovery continues requiring explicit review of its complete executable inventory. Factory mode trusts the validated installed Factory bundle, without asking every project to re-review identical copied files; it still requires existing execution/ownership/eligibility safeguards. Project TOML and instructions are not executable workflow files, but their frozen inputs remain part of run/proof identity.

## CLI, scheduler and Board routing

Use one resolver in cli/src/commands/dispatch.mts and run.mts, cli/src/runs.mts, schedule.mts, commands/schedule.mts and commands/tick.mts. Preserve argv, project cwd, saved scheduler Node/PATH, state propagation, child process groups, logs, exit codes, invocation overrides, pause/off checks and refresh-only restrictions. Remove shared-mode checks for the existence or regex contents of project dispatch/main copies. Apply complete manifest validation instead. Refresh-only never invokes agent implementation, admission or tracker mutation.

Route recovery-run/recovery-review and recovery preparation/image readiness callers through the selected runtime. Preserve pre-charge checks, claim/admission token transfer and exact cleanup. Recovery status/review reports selected runtime identity/mode. A code edit in a project override invalidates review; switching runtime mode cannot reuse a previous project-code review as proof. Board refresh-worker uses the same resolver and project identity, not the existence of .sandcastle/dispatch.mts. Update Factory and standalone Board installation inventories to ship the resolver/parser and a configured descriptor for the runtime store; standalone installation prepares the bundle through the same builder, not its own divergent workflow copy. The Board must fail read-only refresh clearly if its descriptor is unavailable, not execute local code accidentally.

## New project assets and instructions

Change scaffold.mts and init.mts so new Factory-mode projects receive factory.toml v2, .env/.env.example, .gitignore, and empty instruction/helper locations as needed. A tiny factory-dispatch.sh may remain solely as a quoted `exec factory dispatch --project <canonical-root>` convenience wrapper forwarding argv; it contains no implementation and is not a runtime fallback. Do not copy config/main/dispatch, tracker/recovery/Board/parser modules, Factory prompts or runtime package dependencies into projects. Preserve exclusive create/no-overwrite behavior, input validation and safe reruns. Both profiles default to OpenAI; profiles retain their tracker/merge/selection differences, not distinct agents.

Add `orchestrator/instructions.mts` to validate/read/freeze additive Markdown and produce common-then-role text and hashes. Compose instructions into explicit sections in Factory-owned prompt templates; insert file content as literal text, never a second pass of template expansion. Freeze resolved bytes for the invocation/attempt; bind analysis-cache and verification identity to relevant files. Optional absent lists are empty; a configured unreadable/missing file fails before the corresponding agent. Keep read-only analysis and independent verification capabilities unchanged. Default templates retain all mandatory structured-output fields and evidence policy.

Update update.mts for Factory mode: no obsolete missing-code classifications or suggestions to copy default workflow modules; project data is never overwritten; selected runtime is upgraded only through install. For project overrides report project-owned code, not automatically repair it. Do not add a migration/apply command or delete historical project files.

## Read-only explanation

Add `factory config explain [--project <name-or-path>] [--json]` in cli/bin/factory.mts and cli/src/commands/config.mts. Versioned JSON v1 includes projectRoot, config path/schema, workflow mode/root/content identity, normalized ordinary settings with explicit/default sources, family, Factory role/tier model mapping and policy source, configured instruction paths and hashes, and warnings/errors. Show only a summary/count of setup commands and instruction files, not arbitrary command/script/instruction bodies or environment values. Credentials and auth stores are never read. Missing/invalid config/runtime/files produce sanitized key/path diagnostics and exit 1; valid resolved output exits 0. No tracker/Docker/package/network/process/service-manager calls and no runtime preparation, leases or state writes. Complete-override behavior is opaque beyond the validated manifest and declared standard settings; do not claim that arbitrary code honors the standard model mapping.

Update selection explain to use v2 config and runtime identity without importing executable overrides. In project mode show native selection evaluation as configured intent, not an assurance that custom code uses it; custom execution behavior remains unknown. Do not duplicate #156's drift/image/source comparison.

## Tests

Each task adds focused unit/fixture tests with injected command/container/agent boundaries. No live tracker, Docker daemon, auth, npm registry or service manager in acceptance tests.

- Schema: defaults, explicit values, enum/key errors, v1/absent config, old model keys, role/deadline escape hatches, paths/containment and source attribution.
- Models: both families, each tier and role, missing/default tier, valid duplicate/conflicting/invalid tiers, old exact-model fields, ignored code/quotes/comments, frozen active choice and unchanged recovery default.
- Bundles: locked complete copied/link installation, atomic publication/failure, isolation from poisoned project node_modules, dependency installation boundary, stable content identity, active old bundle after new install and ownership-safe uninstall.
- Runtime: two different projects run the same code with different trackers/images/setup/instructions and isolated local artifacts; shared imports never read sibling project or installed sample settings. All detached children retain identity.
- Routing: manual run/dispatch, scheduled dispatch, paused refresh, Board refresh, recovery and any landed preparation/capability/delivery follow-up choose the same configured runtime. Incomplete override never mixes with installed code. Unknown config fails before credentials/Docker/admission. Read-only paths mutate nothing.
- Assets/instructions: minimal scaffold, no copied workflow/deps/prompts, no overwrite, idempotency, literal instruction insertion, role ordering, missing/escaping paths, cache/proof invalidation and exact unchanged mandatory prompt output contracts.
- End-to-end temporary copied-install fixture: initialize a project with no workflow files, run a fake-agent ticket through fixed stages, report identity, exercise independent verification and recovery routing, publish runtime B while A remains active, and test a complete customized workflow plus broken override. All expected actions are recorded by fixture-owned stubs. Verify no fallback to project scripts or project package installs.

Run focused tests, then `node --test orchestrator/*.test.mts board/*.test.mts cli/test/*.test.mts` under TESTING.md. Update obsolete legacy fixtures to explicitly expect unsupported legacy inputs; do not delete safety regression coverage under the excuse of dropping compatibility.

## Task split and dependencies

The task tickets below carry self-contained contracts and exact edit boundaries. The runtime-execution and cross-path routing tasks use the Large model because their respective import/context and admission/process ownership boundaries cannot be delivered safely as disconnected partial edits. Other tasks use Mid. Source/file overlap with queued work is not itself a hard dependency. No queued ticket is edited.

| Task | Pi model | Hard dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Define v2 configuration and Factory model policy | openai/gpt-6.1-terra | None |
| 2. Package immutable shared runtimes and private dependencies | openai/gpt-6.1-terra | None |
| 3. Execute the standard workflow with explicit project context | openai/gpt-6.1-sol | 1, 2 |
| 4. Route CLI, scheduling, recovery and Board through one workflow | openai/gpt-6.1-sol | 3 |
| 5. Create minimal projects and compose additive instructions | openai/gpt-6.1-terra | 3 |
| 6. Explain effective configuration and test complete workflows | openai/gpt-6.1-terra | 4, 5 |
| 7. Document shared execution and customization for users and agents | openai/gpt-6.1-terra | 6 |

The final documentation task is strictly last, after all code and integration tests. Earlier changes still update the docs required by the repository policy effective at implementation time, plus touched-file header comments. Read writing-for-agents before changing the setup skill or agent instructions. At the planning baseline the required guides are README.md, orchestrator/ADAPTING.md and skills/sandcastle-setup/SKILL.md; if #155 lands, follow its approved relevant-document policy instead of recreating blanket edits.

## Deploy and verification boundaries

Implement through Factory in the implementation checkout and isolated fixtures only. Do not alter real installed apps, project copies, registries, schedules/services, credentials or production systems. No 1Password access. This ticket authorizes a source change, not deployment. The owner manually migrates existing projects after release. Preserve original saved work/evidence/budgets; never adopt an old review/proof by guessing compatibility. Publishing new runtime bundles is a future normal install action, not something to do to the user's installation during this implementation.

## Estimate

90 hours human without AI: schema/model policy 10h; runtime packaging/dependency ownership 12h; project-context execution 22h; launch-path/override/recovery integration 20h; minimal scaffold/instructions 10h; effective configuration/end-to-end acceptance 8h; final user/agent documentation 8h. Each includes orientation, implementation, focused tests and review. The final documentation allocation includes full-suite QA and release guidance; no production deployment or manual project migrations are included.

</details>

#161 and #162 can start independently. #164 and #165 can proceed after #163; shared prompt call-site edits belong only to #165's narrow instruction wiring after #163 establishes the interface. #167 is strictly last through its transitive dependencies, as requested.

The seven parent/sub-issue relationships and all seven native blocked-by links were read back from GitHub. The parent is not blocked by its children. Existing ready-for-agent tickets #149, #151, #152 and #153 were reviewed and left unchanged; none produces a contract this work must wait for, beyond preserving any behavior already present on its implementation base. File overlap alone is not a hard dependency.

**Estimate:** 90h human without AI across all seven tasks. This excludes existing-project migration and production deployment.

161.title: Define v2 project settings and Factory model tiers
161.description:
**Pi model:** openai/gpt-6.1-terra
**Part of:** #160
**Depends on:** None

## Goal

Define the breaking v2 project-data contract and the pure Factory-owned family/tier model policy.

## Context

The standard workflow will run Factory code, not project copies. Projects may select one family for all roles, default OpenAI. Pi is the only standard agent: openai family uses Pi provider openai; anthropic uses pi-claude-subscription. Projects cannot configure exact models, aliases, thinking, per-role families or new deadlines. Custom code belongs to a complete workflow override. Existing-project compatibility and migration tooling are explicitly out of scope.

## Changes

- `orchestrator/project-config.mts`: require version=2. Remove executable/legacy fallback from the data contract. Retain every non-AI v1 key, default and eligibility/selection/merge/sandbox semantic. Keep existing graph.analysis_timeout_minutes, sandbox setup timeout_ms and CI waits. Replace agent fields with optional family=openai|anthropic, default openai. Remove graph.model. Reject all superseded keys and unknown nested keys with file/key guidance, without arbitrary source snippets.
- Add optional workflow table: mode=factory|project, default factory. directory is required only in project mode and rejected in factory mode. Add optional instructions arrays common/implementation/verification/analysis/recovery, all default []. Each contains nonempty repository-relative Markdown paths. Export reusable path-validation functions for later runtime/instruction consumers: canonical checkout containment, no absolute/parent-traversal paths or missing/escaping symlinks. Parse-time validation covers shape; filesystem validation belongs to consumers before use. Record explicit/default sources for all settings.
- Absent/v1 config returns an actionable unsupported/manual-migration error for new shared callers. Do not infer shared mode from old copied files or create a converter. Retain a data-only identity helper for callers, with no legacy code import.
- New `orchestrator/model-policy.mts`: export ModelFamily, ModelTier, role selection and immutable policy tables. Small/Mid/Large map respectively to openai/gpt-6-luna, openai/gpt-6.1-terra, openai/gpt-6.1-sol, or pi-claude-subscription/claude-haiku-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-opus-5-5. Analysis uses Mid, verification/recovery Large; thinking is code-owned high. No availability probing or automatic provider/model fallback.
- `orchestrator/models.mts`: add pure tier resolution for standalone Model tier or bold Model tier fields, case-insensitive small/mid/large. Missing => resolved Mid, source=factory-default. Valid explicit => source=ticket-tier. Identical duplicate tiers accepted; conflicting/invalid values held. Preserve current parser exclusions for fenced/indented code, quotes and HTML comments. Active old Model/Pi model declarations fail with guidance, even alongside a valid tier. Do not derive tier from labels/comments/parent/prose. Retain Pi auth/subscription wiring utilities; runtime callers are rewired by the execution task.
- `board/assessment.mts` and `board/board.mts` types where ModelResolution/RunState require it: additive family/tier/source/resolved-model metadata, description revision and policy identity, preserving historical records. Do not rewrite old state or budgets. Update rendering only where new statuses would otherwise be misrepresented.
- `orchestrator/factory.personal.toml` and factory.client.toml: version 2, both default OpenAI, no agent/provider/model aliases/graph.model/thinking; retain profile tracker/selection/merge differences and empty sandbox setup. Add commented workflow/instructions examples. Do not make stages or deadlines configurable.
- `orchestrator/config-read.mts`: v2 scalar bridge derives Pi/subscription/provider facts from family. No credential resolution or arbitrary JSON evaluation.

## Tests

- Extend project-config/model tests for preserved ordinary defaults/filters, both families, omitted agent table, source attribution and v1/absent/unknown/superseded/role/deadline errors.
- New model-policy tests cover every family/tier/role mapping and fixed Pi/thinking policy.
- Tier parser tests cover absent/default, mixed case, bold/plain fields, identical/conflicting/invalid declarations, explicit old model fields, and excluded fenced/quoted/commented examples.
- State/type fixtures preserve readability of old historical records. New choice metadata can be frozen without refresh overwriting it.
- Keep tests offline and import-safe. At this intermediate dependency stage, document affected old callers rather than adding a compatibility fallback; downstream task 3 owns wiring them to v2.

## Done when

- [ ] V2 contains family selection only for AI and preserves all agreed ordinary settings.
- [ ] Exact models and role defaults live in pure Factory code with deterministic tests.
- [ ] Tickets can request tiers without choosing family/model IDs.
- [ ] No legacy execution, new deadlines, migrations or deployed-project changes are introduced.

## Documentation and verification

Update the docs required by the effective repository policy in this change, including touched-file headers. Planning baseline requires README.md, orchestrator/ADAPTING.md and skills/sandcastle-setup/SKILL.md; if #155 lands, use its approved relevant-document rule. Read writing-for-agents before skill edits. Final consolidated documentation remains the last epic task. Use temporary fixtures, no real auth/tracker/Docker/services/1Password/production. Run focused tests and retain safety regressions; final full-suite integration belongs to task 6.

**Estimate:** 10h human without AI, including implementation, tests and review.

162.title: Package stable Factory runtimes with private dependencies
162.description:
**Pi model:** openai/gpt-6.1-terra
**Part of:** #160
**Depends on:** None

## Goal

Prepare complete Factory runtime bundles with private locked dependencies, and keep active code stable across installs.

## Context

Today init copies the workflow into each project and dispatch installs @ai-hero/sandcastle/tsx into the target project's node_modules. The new standard workflow must use an installed Factory-owned runtime and never resolve execution dependencies from a target project. Projects will not pin versions, and existing-project migration is out of scope. This task owns packaging, not workflow execution rewiring or new-project scaffolding.

## Changes

- New `cli/src/runtime-assets.mts`: one versioned assembly inventory for a complete flat runtime. Map orchestrator modules, required Board/admission/assessment/journal helpers, vendored TOML parser and Factory-owned prompts to runtime-relative paths. Start from cli/src/scaffold.mts FROM_ORCHESTRATOR/FROM_BOARD plus main.mts and prompts, without copying project config.mts or project-specific legacy CONFIG values. Prompt sources are cli/templates/project/prompt.md and prompt.verify.md plus orchestrator/prompt.analyze.md and prompt.recover.md. Include every transitive executable helper present on the implementation base. Export inventory/manifest validation for later routing and review consumers. Do not independently maintain a second copy list.
- New `cli/src/runtime-bundle.mts`: prepare `<Factory data>/runtimes/<content-id>/` from a temporary sibling. Include package.json/package-lock.json for the root locked @ai-hero/sandcastle and tsx dependencies, and install privately with npm ci --include=dev --ignore-scripts. No project cwd/node_modules/npm mutation, no global package resolution and no install at ticket launch. Inject package installation in tests. Verify locked package behavior under the existing supported Node floor.
- The versioned manifest records sorted relative source hashes, package/lock hash, Node compatibility and deterministic content identity. This is local content identity, not a fabricated release or signature. Validate all relative destinations, symlinks and collisions before copying. Fail on missing or incomplete sources. Publish atomically after successful preparation; reuse an already validated identical bundle. Never patch published bundles in place.
- `cli/src/paths.mts`, commands/install.mts and manifest.mts: install first prepares the bundle, then atomically updates an installed-app runtime descriptor. Keep the old descriptor usable if bundle preparation fails. Retain the existing app/source ownership checks and scheduler-off behavior. Both copied and --link installs select a prepared bundle outside the replaceable p.app directory. Link mode requires reinstall to publish new runtime source; editing linked source must not mutate active runtime code.
- Export descriptor reader and lease helpers: a lease binds bundle id to owner PID/start identity, with current ownership patterns and exclusive local writes. A subsequent install does not delete older bundles. Downstream launchers will acquire/transfer leases. No automatic GC, per-project pins or age-only stale-owner theft.
- `cli/src/commands/uninstall.mts` and manifest validation: record the runtime store as an exactly owned path, never a generic deletion allowance. Refuse deletion of live referenced bundles; preserve unknown-ownership bundles with an explicit error rather than deleting them. Preserve manifest path-containment checks.
- Update install/test packaging inventories so prompts, parser, package manifests and runtime builder survive copied installs. Do not modify the actual user's installed app or invoke a real scheduler.

## Tests

- Add cli/test/runtime-bundle.test.mts for complete manifest, deterministic identity, changed-source/lock identity, missing assets, symlink escapes, collisions, failed install, partial publication, concurrent identical preparation and an unchanged old descriptor after failure.
- Copied and linked install fixtures produce independent prepared runtimes. Publish B while a fixture-owned process holds A and prove A's sources/dependency paths remain usable. Live/unknown leases prevent unsafe deletion; confirmed dead ownership follows existing PID/start-identity semantics.
- Poison a fake target project's node_modules and npm scripts; preparing a runtime must neither resolve from nor execute them.
- Assert npm registry/process boundaries with injected stub installation. Do not contact npm, Docker, trackers, credentials or service managers in tests.
- Existing install/uninstall/manifest safety fixtures remain green. Integration launch-path tests are downstream, not a reason to weaken packaging validation.

## Done when

- [ ] Install publishes a complete stable runtime with private locked dependencies.
- [ ] Subsequent installs cannot replace code underneath a live runtime consumer.
- [ ] Bundle identity/descriptor/leases have offline tests and explicit failure behavior.
- [ ] No target-project code or dependencies are installed or migrated.

## Documentation and verification

Update effective-policy docs and touched-file headers in the same change. Planning baseline requires README.md, orchestrator/ADAPTING.md and skills/sandcastle-setup/SKILL.md; follow #155's relevant-document rule instead if it has landed. Read writing-for-agents before skill edits. Final guide consolidation is the last epic task. Implement only in source and isolated fixtures, not real installs/services/projects/auth or production; no 1Password.

**Estimate:** 12h human without AI, including implementation, tests and review.
